object_types.name: Account
object_types.definition: A customer in the system; every account has an account number and everything hangs off it.

source_references.excerpt: An account. Every account has an account number. That's what everything hangs off.

object_types.name: AccountNumber
object_types.definition: Six digit sequential identifier for an account, never reused.

source_references.excerpt: Six digits, sequential, never reused.

object_types.name: Subscription
object_types.definition: The agreement that an account pays a given amount on a given cycle for a given product; identified by a subscription ID.

source_references.excerpt: A subscription is the agreement that this account pays us this amount on this cycle for this thing. It's got a subscription ID.

object_types.name: SubscriptionId
object_types.definition: Generated unique identifier for a subscription, prefixed with SUB.

source_references.excerpt: Unique. Generated, prefixed with SUB.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: One of the products sold, identified by a product code.

source_references.excerpt: Product code. We have three: CORE, ANALYTICS, and CONNECT.
Product code. We have three: CORE, ANALYTICS, and CONNECT.

object_types.name: PricePlan
object_types.definition: The billing artefact that says what the customer pays and how often; identified by a plan code.

source_references.excerpt: The price plan. It's got a plan code, it says what the customer pays and how often. CORE-MO-49, CORE-AN-490, that kind of thing.

object_types.name: PlanCode
object_types.definition: Code identifying a price plan, e.g. CORE-MO-49.

source_references.excerpt: CORE-MO-49, CORE-AN-490, that kind of thing.

object_types.name: FeatureBundle
object_types.definition: The feature bundle a customer gets -- what the customer gets in terms of seats, API, SSO; identified by its unique name (Starter, Professional, Enterprise).

source_references.excerpt: When I say plan I mean what the customer gets. Starter, Professional, Enterprise. It's the feature bundle -- how many seats, whether they get the API, whether they get SSO.
Name. Starter, Professional, Enterprise. There's no code, which annoys me. ... Yes. There's exactly one Professional.
Start date is always there. You can't create a subscription without one, the form won't submit.
An open-ended subscription has no end date. Most of them are open-ended -- they run until cancelled.

object_types.name: BillingPeriod
object_types.definition: The billing cycle of a subscription: monthly or annual.

source_references.excerpt: Monthly or annual.

object_types.name: SubscriptionStatus
object_types.definition: The status of a subscription: trialing, active, past due, or cancelled.

source_references.excerpt: Trialing, active, past due, cancelled.

object_types.name: PausedFlag
object_types.definition: A separate boolean flag indicating a subscription is paused; overlaps confusingly with status.

source_references.excerpt: Paused isn't a status, it's a flag. ... it's a separate boolean, which is exactly why it causes bugs.

object_types.name: PlanChange
object_types.definition: A record of a change to a subscription's price plan, with an effective date and requester; belongs to exactly one subscription.

source_references.excerpt: A change is a record. We don't overwrite the plan on the subscription, we write a plan change with an effective date... It's got a change ID.

object_types.name: ChangeId
object_types.definition: Identifier for a plan change record.

source_references.excerpt: It's got a change ID.

object_types.name: EffectiveDate
object_types.definition: The date on which a plan change takes effect.

source_references.excerpt: It has to, because we need to know who made it and when it takes effect, and those are different dates.

object_types.name: Requester
object_types.definition: The person who requested a plan change.

source_references.excerpt: It records the subscription, the new price plan, the effective date, and who requested it.

object_types.name: MRR
object_types.definition: Monthly recurring revenue; derived value, not stored, computed from price plan price normalised to a month.

source_references.excerpt: Every subscription has an MRR. Monthly recurring revenue. ... It's worked out. It's the plan price normalised to a month.

ambiguities.description: The word 'plan' is used for at least three distinct concepts: the billing PricePlan, the product FeatureBundle, and a sales-negotiated deal. The sales-negotiated 'plan' is mentioned but explicitly deferred to another meeting and not modeled here. Confirm no further modeling is needed for the sales deal concept.

source_references.excerpt: So we've got two things both called plan. ... the sales team calls a third thing a plan, which is the deal they negotiated, which frequently matches neither.

ambiguities.description: MRR is described as derived from 'the plan price normalised to a month' but the underlying stored price value/amount on PricePlan is never explicitly modeled as a value type (e.g. 'PricePlanAmount'). Need to confirm price amount is a first-class attribute of PricePlan to support MRR derivation.

source_references.excerpt: It's the plan price normalised to a month. An annual plan at 490 is an MRR of 40.83. ... So it's derived from the price plan and the billing period.

ambiguities.description: The PausedFlag is described as overlapping confusingly with SubscriptionStatus (paused subscriptions are returned when querying for 'active'). It's unclear whether this is a known bug to be preserved as-is in the model or a business rule requiring correction (e.g., should paused imply a specific status value, or is it an independent orthogonal flag). Clarify intended relationship between PausedFlag and SubscriptionStatus.

source_references.excerpt: There's also paused. ... It behaves like a status but it isn't one, it's a separate boolean, which is exactly why it causes bugs. If you ask the system for active subscriptions you get paused ones too.

ambiguities.description: The commercial policy for mid-term cancellation of annual subscriptions (run to term vs prorated refund vs credit) is explicitly undecided and parked by the facilitator. No constraint has been modeled for refund/credit behavior; confirm this should remain unmodeled until business/legal decide.

source_references.excerpt: What happens commercially when an annual subscription is cancelled mid-term -- run to term, prorated refund, or credit -- is undecided.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether the current PricePlan field on Subscription must always be consistent with the latest PlanChange record, or whether discrepancies (bugs) are expected and how they should be resolved structurally. The transcript states 'if those two ever disagree, the change history wins and the current plan is the bug' -- this suggests a business rule/constraint (equality or derivation) between current plan and latest plan change that is not fully formalized.

source_references.excerpt: And if those two ever disagree, the change history wins and the current plan is the bug.

ambiguities.description: When an account closes and the same company returns, it receives a new account number and is treated as a new customer, losing history. It's unclear whether any entity should represent the 'company' independent of Account to preserve continuity, or whether this is intentionally out of scope.

source_references.excerpt: If an account closes and the same company comes back, they get a new number and we treat them as a new customer for reporting. ... Which drives me mad, incidentally, because from a product perspective it's the same company and we lose the history.

ambiguities.description: The fourth product is 'in discovery' and not yet defined; ProductCode value_constraint currently lists only three values (CORE, ANALYTICS, CONNECT) which may need to be revisited when the fourth product is finalized.

source_references.excerpt: Fixed today. There's a fourth in discovery, but I'm not going to pretend I know what it is.

ambiguities.description: It's unclear whether Subscription's link to Account, Product, and PricePlan should be modeled as three separate binary mandatory/unique fact types or as a single ternary/quaternary fact type as currently modeled; the transcript states each subscription belongs to exactly one account, product, and price plan but does not clarify whether product is derivable from price plan (since price plans appear to be product-specific, e.g. CORE-MO-49). This may introduce redundancy between Subscription-Product and Subscription-PricePlan-FeatureBundle relationships.

source_references.excerpt: A subscription is identified by a subscription ID, and belongs to exactly one account, one product, and one price plan.
